panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). in_text_mentions: On examination, he was vitally stable. He looked undernourished even though his weight was on the 90th centile, likely due to ascites. Abdominal examination revealed mild ascites, normal bowel sounds, and no organomegaly. Cardiac and respiratory examinations were unremarkable. His right foot showed almost no edema. Left foot examination revealed a significantly swollen dorsal aspect of the foot and toes confirming presence of edema up to the level of his ankle. The edema was minimally pitting, with a positive Stemmer’s sign (Fig. 1). Ankle joint examination was otherwise unremarkable.
